title: Monotonicity of extended power means
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $a\le b\le1$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative. Then $M_a(f)\le M_b(f)$, where $M_p$ is the extended power mean under the uniform measure.
replaced: Let $a\le b\le1$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $M_a(f)\le M_b(f)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform.
